In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the orthology relation contains much more information than just the gene and species trees, and that this information can be used for a variety of purposes, including the detection of horizontal gene transfer events and the estimation of gene duplication times.

, while the orthology problem is NP-hard, it is not NP-complete, in that there is a polynomial time algorithm that solves it in the case where the underlying orthology relation can be represented as a symbolic ultrametric.
the orthology relation is not only a powerful tool for reconstructing phylogenetic trees, but also for detecting and understanding phylogenetic conflicts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that orthology detection can be seen as a special case of cograph recognition.
orthology relations can be viewed as a special kind of symbolic ultrametrics.
the orthology relation is a symbolic ultrametric if and only if there exists a cograph whose vertices are labeled with the genes and whose edges correspond to pairs of genes that are orthologs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the context of orthology detection, the problem of inferring gene trees and species trees from orthology relations is equivalent to that of reconstructing the gene tree from the orthology relation, given the species tree.
, although orthology relations are in general very difficult to analyze, they do have certain properties that can be used to recover some of the relevant phylogenetic information.
, in principle, orthology detection methods that are based on gene trees and species trees can be improved by using the orthology relation as a starting point, rather than the other way around.
